Upwardly Global is a U.S.-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization formed in 2000, that provides career coaching and employment services to immigrant and refugee professionals. The organization is headquartered in New York City, with additional offices in San Francisco, Chicago, and Washington, D.C.
History
Upwardly Global was founded in 2000 by Jane Leu in San Francisco, California.
In 2009, Leu stepped down as CEO and joined the board of directors. Nikki Cicerani served as executive director from 2009 to 2018, during which the organization expanded from two to four metropolitan areas and launched virtual services in 2013.
Jina Krause-Vilmar served as president and CEO from 2018 to 2025. In December 2025, Upwardly Global announced the appointment of Gregory Adam Haile as CEO. Haile assumed the role in January 2026. He previously served as president of Broward College from 2018 to 2023 and is an equity partner at Strategos Group, where he founded his Higher Education and Workforce Advisory practice. He is also a senior fellow at the Mossavar-Rahmani Center for Business and Government at the Harvard Kennedy School and serves as board chair of the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta.
Programs
Career Coaching Program
Upwardly Global offers a free career coaching program for immigrant and refugee professionals. The program provides one-on-one coaching, job search assistance, resume support, interview preparation, and skills training to help participants navigate the U.S. job market. Participants also receive access to online learning platforms, including Coursera, Cisco Networking Academy, and eCornell.
In 2022, Upwardly Global partnered with employers and organizations in Poland to provide career coaching services to displaced Ukrainian professionals.
Partnership Model
Upwardly Global partners with workforce agencies, educational institutions, and other nonprofit organizations and provides them with tools and training to support immigrants and refugees in their job searches. Services include professional development for coaches, technical assistance, and access to Upwardly Global’s online learning platform.
Partners include the New York State Office for New Americans, Welcome Back Initiative, and Global Detroit.
Employer Engagement
Upwardly Global works with midsize and Fortune 500 companies to support the hiring of foreign-born candidates and the development of returnship and mid-career internship programs. It also organizes employee mentorship and volunteer opportunities.
Partners include Accenture, JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Cisco, and Deloitte.
Advocacy
In 2023, Upwardly Global worked with the Illinois State Medical Society, the Chicago Bilingual Nurse Consortium, and State Rep. Theresa Mah to develop legislation creating a new medical licensing pathway for internationally trained doctors in Illinois. The law created a limited license allowing foreign-trained physicians to practice under a supervising doctor for two years, followed by a provisional license for an additional two years, before receiving a full unrestricted license. The law went into effect in 2025.
Upwardly Global is a member organization of the Evacuate Our Allies (EOA) Coalition and has advocated for the Afghan Adjustment Act, which would provide lawful permanent resident status to certain Afghan nationals paroled into the United States.
Technology
In 2021, Upwardly Global released an AI-based job pathways tool to help immigrants navigate U.S. job searches. In 2024, with funding from Cisco, the organization added a career navigation assistant and an AI-powered resume builder.
In 2023, Upwardly Global partnered with HiredScore to develop AI tools intended to reduce bias in automated hiring systems. This partnership resulted in Upwardly Global Fetch, a custom API integration with Workday's HiredScore AI recruiting tool. The integration pulls candidate profiles from Upwardly Global's database directly into recruiters' existing Workday workflows. In an initial analysis, the tool surfaced 575 candidate recommendations for open roles from a pool of 1,500 immigrant job seekers.
Funding
Upwardly Global's first grant was awarded in 2002. The organization has since received funding from sources including the Achelis Foundation, Ashoka: Innovators for the Public, GitLab Foundation, Siegel Family Foundation, Western Union Foundation, the Eric and Wendy Schmidt Fund for Strategic Innovations, among others.
In 2024, the organization received a philanthropic gift from MacKenzie Scott's foundation, Yield Giving.
Recognition
Upwardly Global has received several awards, including the 2004 Manhattan Institute Award for Social Entrepreneurship,  the Migration Policy Institute's 2010 E Pluribus Unum Award, and a Bronze Anthem Community Voice award for their work supporting Ukrainian refugees in Poland. The organization received honorable mentions in Fast Company's 2023 World Changing Ideas Awards and Ragan's Crisis Communications Awards for its response to Operation Allies Welcome, which assisted Afghan newcomers.
